capabilities.name: Core MCP
capabilities.rationale: Seed the must-be surface: CRUD, data model, primary API contract — the tools without which the product is broken.
capabilities.description: Core MCP tools. Must-be functionality (Kano 2).
capabilities.gherkin: Rule: Every core tool must be idempotent-safe and return valid JSON on success and failure.

capabilities.name: Auxiliary MCP
capabilities.rationale: Extract the supporting surface you survive a day without — validation, batch ops, product-specific GitHub integration.
capabilities.description: Auxiliary MCP tools. Must-be but not critical-path (Kano 3).
capabilities.gherkin: Rule: Auxiliary tools must not corrupt data if they fail mid-operation.

capabilities.name: Performance MCP
capabilities.rationale: Enforce measurable improvement: more is better — latency, throughput, accuracy, coverage tools that move a number.
capabilities.description: Performance MCP tools. Linear-satisfaction dimensions (Kano 4).
capabilities.gherkin: Rule: Performance tools must report a quantitative result; qualitative output belongs in Auxiliary MCP.

capabilities.name: CLI
capabilities.rationale: Inherit terminal ergonomics — a thin wrapper over MCP tools so power users stay in the shell.
capabilities.description: Command-line interface. Thin wrapper — all logic lives in MCP tools.
capabilities.gherkin: Rule: CLI commands must map 1:1 to MCP tool calls with no additional business logic.

capabilities.name: Spec CRUD UI
capabilities.rationale: Mirror backend Cap 1 in the browser — reveal create/read/update/delete surfaces so visual users never drop to the CLI for basic spec work.
capabilities.description: UI mirror of Cap 1 (Core MCP). Features grow one-to-one with backend CRUD features as they ship. Empty at scaffold — populated per backend Cap 1 as it grows.
capabilities.gherkin: Rule: Every feature here mirrors a Cap 1 feature; no UI surface exists without a backend tool to drive it.

capabilities.name: Spec Lifecycle UI
capabilities.rationale: Mirror backend Cap 2 in the browser — reveal lifecycle transitions (approve, challenge, restore, tidy) as visual affordances.
capabilities.description: UI mirror of Cap 2 (Auxiliary MCP — lifecycle). Features grow one-to-one with backend lifecycle features as they ship. Empty at scaffold — populated per backend Cap 2 as it grows.
capabilities.gherkin: Rule: Every feature here mirrors a Cap 2 feature; no UI surface exists without a backend tool to drive it.

capabilities.name: Help & Assist UI
capabilities.rationale: Mirror backend Cap 3 in the browser — reveal AI suggestions, gherkin generation, and scoring surfaces users would otherwise invoke by tool name.
capabilities.description: UI mirror of Cap 3 (Performance MCP — AI assist and scoring). Features grow one-to-one with backend assist features as they ship. Empty at scaffold — populated per backend Cap 3 as it grows.
capabilities.gherkin: Rule: Every feature here mirrors a Cap 3 feature; no UI surface exists without a backend tool to drive it.

capabilities.name: Web UI
capabilities.rationale: Inherit the cross-cutting browser shell — navigation, settings, shared chrome that isn't tied to one backend cap.
capabilities.description: Product-specific cross-cutting UI shell + settings. Distinct from the UI-mirror caps at 5/6/7 which mirror a single backend cap each.
capabilities.gherkin: Rule: Shell-level UI actions must call an MCP tool — no server-side logic outside MCP.

capabilities.name: Behind the Scenes
capabilities.rationale: Record the invisible-to-customer mechanics that keep the product alive — background jobs, caches, retries.
capabilities.description: Invisible infrastructure. Not Kano-rated (no customer-visible satisfaction dimension).
capabilities.gherkin: Rule: Behaviors here must cite the customer-facing cap they serve; infrastructure without a beneficiary is deleted.

capabilities.name: KPI Calculation
capabilities.rationale: Distill how numbers on dashboards get made — KPI pipelines are abstract; document them here, not in the UI.
capabilities.description: KPI derivation specs. Not Kano-rated (abstract benefit, no direct customer satisfaction).
capabilities.gherkin: Rule: Every KPI has a behavior documenting its source data, formula, and refresh cadence.

capabilities.name: Intake
capabilities.rationale: Gate external change requests — triage, sharpen, dedup, classify; nothing graduates without a Kano level.
capabilities.description: Incoming spec change requests from external modules (iris-qa, quartermaster, other agents). Requests land here for triage (sharpen + dedup + kano classification) before promotion into Caps 1-4. See skill create-spec-item.
capabilities.gherkin: Rule: Every intake item names its source agent, proposed Kano level, and target cap before promotion.

capabilities.name: Shared Components
capabilities.rationale: Inherit shared MCP tools (github auth, settings, health, switch_repo) and shared UI components from Architrix — not re-specified per product.
capabilities.description: Ecosystem-shared infrastructure: shared MCP tools and shared React/UI components inherited from Architrix.
capabilities.gherkin: Rule: Shared Components behaviors are identical across all ecosystem services; product-specific overrides live in their product cap.

capabilities.name: Technical Specifications
capabilities.rationale: Enforce architecture decisions with testable contracts — ADRs with Gherkin, not PDFs.
capabilities.description: ADRs for runtime, security, data storage, and infrastructure decisions. Debug & Observability reserves a standard feature slot here; it is NOT its own capability.

features.name: Security
features.rationale: Guard product-wide security decisions: encryption, auth factors, access control.

features.name: Runtime & Stack
features.rationale: Fix the runtime perimeter: language, framework, containerization.

features.name: Data Storage
features.rationale: Enforce persistence strategy — storage engine, backup, migration.
features.description: Storage engine, backup strategy, migration approach.

capabilities.gherkin: Rule: Technical decisions must be documented as behaviors with testable acceptance criteria.

capabilities.name: Design Specs
capabilities.rationale: Enforce a consistent visual language — tokens, not one-off hex codes.
capabilities.description: Typography, color palette, layout patterns, and reusable components. Renamed from 'Design System' in Phase 13 to match canonical ecosystem naming.
capabilities.gherkin: Rule: All UI components must use design-specs tokens — no hardcoded colors or font sizes.

capabilities.name: QA Specs
capabilities.rationale: Seal the test-tool contract — Cap 12.1 setup, 12.2 teardown, 12.3 QA tool contract.
capabilities.description: Test tool contract: Cap 12.1 setup, Cap 12.2 teardown, Cap 12.3 QA tool contract. QA-testable Gherkin targets Cap 100 sandbox, not product caps.
capabilities.gherkin: Rule: QA behaviors target the Cap 100 sandbox; product caps are never mutated by tests.

capabilities.name: Less is More
capabilities.rationale: Guard the product from bloat: things we REMOVED or kept OUT to make the rest shine.
capabilities.description: Kano 6 slot — features whose absence is the feature. Empty placeholder.
capabilities.gherkin: Rule: Entries here must name the thing removed and the user problem removal solves.

capabilities.name: Me Too
capabilities.rationale: Match the table-stakes competitors expose — MVP-only, no polish, no investment beyond parity.
capabilities.description: Kano 7 slot — parity features users won't switch for but will miss. Empty placeholder.
capabilities.gherkin: Rule: Entries here exist because a competitor has them; scope is minimal parity, not leadership.

capabilities.name: Nice to Have
capabilities.rationale: Distill low-priority ideas worth keeping in sight but not on the roadmap.
capabilities.description: Kano 8 slot — backlog of non-critical enhancements. Empty placeholder.
capabilities.gherkin: Rule: Entries here carry no commitment; they graduate out or get killed.

capabilities.name: Single Customer
capabilities.rationale: Quarantine features requested by one customer — kill the entry when usage drops to zero.
capabilities.description: Kano 9 slot — per-customer specials. Empty placeholder.
capabilities.gherkin: Rule: Every entry names the single customer and the removal trigger.

capabilities.name: Show Horse
capabilities.rationale: Flag demo-only work — all show, no work; kill when the demo is over.
capabilities.description: Kano 10 slot — items that exist for the demo and nothing else. Empty placeholder.
capabilities.gherkin: Rule: Entries here name the demo they support and the date they expire.
